courses.name: A1 Grammar: Clear Rules with Nguyen Minh Ha
courses.description: Rule-first A1 grammar with worked examples and controlled practice for everyday life.

topics.name: Clear Rules: People and Pronouns
topics.description: Build a reliable subject-pronoun foundation before making sentences.

lessons.title: Personal Pronouns: Name the Person
lessons.description: Learn I, you, he, she, it, we, and they with clear rules and familiar examples.
lessons.content: Use I for the speaker, you for the listener, he for a man or boy, she for a woman or girl, it for a thing or animal, we for the speaker and another person, and they for more than one person. Examples: I carry a bag. She reads a book. They live nearby.

questions.questionText: ___ am in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: I is the subject pronoun for the speaker.

questions.questionText: Mai is my sister. ___ is kind.
questions.explanation: Use she for one female person.

questions.questionText: Tom and I are classmates. ___ study together.
questions.explanation: We means the speaker and another person.

questions.questionText: The keys are on the desk. ___ are not in my bag.
questions.explanation: They refers to more than one thing.

questions.questionText: Anna, can ___ open the window, please?
questions.explanation: You is the pronoun for the person being spoken to.

topics.name: Clear Rules: The Verb Be
topics.description: Practice affirmative, negative, and question forms of be.

lessons.title: Present Be: Statements and Questions
lessons.description: Use am, is, and are in short everyday statements, negatives, and questions.
lessons.content: Use am with I, is with he, she, and it, and are with you, we, and they. Add not for a negative: She is not late. Put be before the subject in a question: Are they ready? Contractions include I'm, isn't, and aren't.

questions.questionText: I ___ ready for class.
questions.explanation: The present form of be used with I is am.

questions.questionText: The shop ___ open today.
questions.explanation: A singular thing uses is.

questions.questionText: We ___ not late for the meeting.
questions.explanation: We takes are, and not makes the sentence negative.

questions.questionText: ___ she your new teacher?
questions.explanation: A question with she begins with is.

questions.questionText: They are not busy. The short form is: ___
questions.explanation: Are not contracts to aren't.

courses.name: A1 Grammar: English in Everyday Dialogues with Tran Quoc Anh
courses.description: Situation-led A1 grammar through short dialogues, pattern noticing, and simple exchanges.

topics.name: Dialogue Patterns: Who Is Speaking?
topics.description: Notice pronouns in short conversations at home, school, and work.

lessons.title: Meet the People: Pronouns in Conversation
lessons.description: Follow short exchanges and replace names with the correct subject pronoun.
lessons.content: Notice the speaker in each exchange. When Linh says, 'I am a student,' I means Linh. When Nam answers, 'You are my friend,' you means the listener. For two people together use we; for a group use they. Example: 'Where are the bags?' 'They are here.'

questions.questionText: Linh says, “___ am a student.”
questions.explanation: The speaker uses I to talk about herself.

questions.questionText: Nam says to you, “___ are my friend.”
questions.explanation: Nam uses you for the person he is speaking to.

questions.questionText: Lan and I are at the bus stop. ___ are waiting.
questions.explanation: The speaker and Lan are together, so we is correct.

questions.questionText: A: Where are the children? B: ___ are in the garden.
questions.explanation: They replaces the plural noun children.

questions.questionText: A: Where is the radio? B: ___ is on the table.
questions.explanation: It replaces the singular thing, the radio.

topics.name: Dialogue Patterns: Be in Real Exchanges
topics.description: Notice am, is, and are while people ask and answer simple questions.

lessons.title: At the Café: Be in Short Exchanges
lessons.description: Use affirmative, negative, and question forms of be in friendly café conversations.
lessons.content: Listen for the subject before be. 'I am hungry' uses am; 'The coffee is hot' uses is; 'We are early' uses are. In a question, be comes first: 'Are you ready?' In a negative reply, use not: 'No, I am not.'

questions.questionText: A: How ___ you today? B: I am fine.
questions.explanation: The question addresses you, so it uses are.

questions.questionText: A: Is the soup hot? B: Yes, it ___.
questions.explanation: It takes the present form is.

questions.questionText: A: Are you tired? B: No, I ___ not.
questions.explanation: The negative answer with I uses am not.

questions.questionText: A: Who is at the door? B: We ___ here.
questions.explanation: We takes are in the present tense.

questions.questionText: A: Are they ready? B: No, they ___.
questions.explanation: They are not ready is the negative answer.
